elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Developed Software and all writings or works of authorship created by M&I remain M&I's property, even if paid for by Customer.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment to Customer is provided; ownership is expressly retained by M&I.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 17.2 denies Customer rights in M&I software, systems, documentation, procedures, and related materials, subject to the express licences.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The perpetual licence covers Developed Software itself, not Vendor IP embedded in Customer-owned Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The irrevocable licence covers Developed Software itself, not Vendor IP embedded in Customer-owned Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The royalty-free licence covers Developed Software itself, not Vendor IP embedded in Customer-owned Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 17.1 states that Customer remains the sole and exclusive owner of all Customer Data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 17.4 expressly requires M&I to use and process Customer Data solely to provide the Services.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The covered property is allocated exclusively: Developed Software to M&I and Customer Data to Customer; no joint ownership is created.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: M&I retains ownership of its programs, ideas, know-how, concepts, systems, and related materials.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: M&I grants Customer a perpetual licence to Developed Software.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: M&I grants Customer an irrevocable licence to Developed Software.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: M&I grants Customer a worldwide licence to Developed Software.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: M&I grants Customer a royalty-free licence to Developed Software.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The licence expressly permits Customer to use and modify Developed Software for Customer's business.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The licence expressly permits Customer to sublicense Developed Software for Customer's business.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Section 17.4 expressly limits M&I's use and processing of Customer Data solely to providing the Services.
